analysis_steps.goal: Self-calibrate and image Stokes I, Q, U, V mosaic

evidence.quote: We note that the individual Stokes I, Q, and U maps from each field are identical to the the final mosaic observations

analysis_steps.goal: Derive debiased polarization intensity, angle, and fraction

method.value: P = sqrt(Q²+U²−σ²); theta = 0.5 atan(U/Q); P_F = P/I; b-vectors by 90° rotation

evidence.quote: The polarization intensity is determined from $\mbox{$\mathcal{P}_I$}= \sqrt{Q^2 + U^2}$.

key_parameters.value: vectors shown for I>3σ and P>4σ; black for >5σ

evidence.quote: We show the e-vectors and b-vectors for regions with $I > 3\ \sigma_I$ and $\mbox{$\mathcal{P}_I$}> 4\ \mbox{$\sigma_{\mathcal{P}I}$}$

assumptions.value: σ_PI ≈ σ_Q ≈ σ_U; 0.1% instrumental polarization uncertainty

evidence.quote: We adopt a polarization fraction uncertainty of 0.1% for the instrument polarization.

validation.value: Stokes V not used because two fields gave inconsistent values

evidence.quote: we do not use the Stokes V data in this study.

analysis_steps.goal: Identify filaments and measure field-filament angle

method.value: FilFinder2D skeleton with user-defined mask; angle difference between skeleton slope and b-vectors; Bridge fitted with y=sqrt(x)

evidence.quote: We use the filament-finding algorithm FilFinder2D (cite: KochRosolowsky15) to produce a skeleton diagram of all filamentary structures in IRAS 16293.

key_parameters.value: mask I>5σ, cuts I<9σ and I<12σ in places

evidence.quote: The user-defined mask is constructed using a mask of $I > 5\ \sigma_I$

fitting.value: y = sqrt(x) curve fitted to southern Bridge skeleton

evidence.quote: we fit a simple $y = \sqrt{x}$ curve to the skeleton.

validation.value: Skeleton compared by eye with Stokes I; thresholds chosen so skeleton traces curvature

evidence.quote: By eye, the skeleton outline has good agreement with the Stokes I emission.

analysis_steps.goal: Compare angle distributions to Monte Carlo field models

method.value: Cumulative angle difference compared with projected random 3-D vectors in 0-20° to 0-90° subsamples; KS and AD tests

evidence.quote: we conduct the two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) test (cite: Kolmogorov33; Smirnov48; Massey51) and the Anderson-Darling (AD) test
we generate a large Monte Carlo sample of 100,000 randomly defined 3-D vectors

assumptions.value: Filaments lie in the plane of the sky

evidence.quote: we assume that the filamentary structures are all in the plane-of-the-sky

evidence.quote: even if we undersample the observations by taking only one data point per beam

analysis_steps.goal: Estimate Bridge mass, density, and field strength

method.value: Modified blackbody mass from average of 85 slices; DCF B = Q sqrt(4πρ) σv/σθ

evidence.quote: We convert this thermal dust emission to mass and column density following a modified blackbody function

evidence.quote: The average slice has a median flux density of 3.4 mJy beam$^{-1}$ and a FWHM of $0.96$$''$ (134 au).

assumptions.value: T = 30 K, kappa = 0.01112 cm2/g, gas-to-dust 100, mu = 2.8, cylinder geometry, Q=0.5

evidence.quote: a gas to dust ratio of 100

fitting.value: Gaussian fit to peak of angle distribution for σθ ≈ 5°; standard deviation of full distribution for 17°

evidence.quote: If we exclude these twisted vectors and fit a Gaussian to the peak distribution, we find $\sigma_{\theta} \approx 5$.

findings_qualitative.value: The inferred field is parallel to the Bridge, A-Streamer and B-Streamer, mostly within 30° of the filaments

evidence.quote: the magnetic field morphology is primarily oriented within 30 of the filamentary structures in IRAS 16293

findings_qualitative.value: Depolarization zone passes through the Bridge near the midpoint

evidence.quote: This depolarization zone spans roughly one beam and passes through the Bridge near the center point between the two stars.

findings_qualitative.value: IRAS 16293B polarization morphology resembles dust self-scattering in a face-on disk, matching 6.9 mm

evidence.quote: Qualitatively, the polarization signature toward IRAS 16293B is reminiscent of dust self-scattering in a face-on disk

claims.hypothesis: Is the field in the filamentary structures parallel or perpendicular to them?
claims.experiment: FilFinder2D skeletons compared with b-vector angles; Monte Carlo, KS and AD tests
claims.result: B-Streamer consistent with <30° distribution (p≈0.4-0.5); random and perpendicular rejected (p≪1e-10); A-Streamer and Bridge more complex
claims.finding: Field is mainly parallel to the Bridge and streamers

evidence.quote: Thus, the magnetic field morphologies of the filamentary structures are mainly parallel

claims.hypothesis: How strong is the field in the Bridge?
claims.experiment: DCF method with measured density, σv and σθ
claims.finding: Field strength estimated, but density is highly uncertain

evidence.quote: As mentioned above, the Bridge density is highly uncertain and could be overestimated by our assumed temperature and dust opacity.

claims.hypothesis: Can the magnetic field regulate gas flow in the Bridge, and is the Bridge long-lived?
claims.experiment: Toy model with stars dominating potential
claims.result: Flow ~1 km/s comparable to Alfvén speed; depletion time ~1e3 yr
claims.finding: Field may regulate flow; Bridge either accretes new material or is transient

evidence.quote: We also find that the bridging material should be depleted in $\sim 10^3$ yr.

claims.hypothesis: What produces the polarization toward IRAS 16293B?
claims.experiment: Compare 1.3 mm ALMA with 6.9 mm VLA and 878 μm SMA polarization
claims.result: Consistent patterns across wavelengths, azimuthal at periphery and uniform at center
claims.finding: Qualitatively consistent with dust self-scattering, implying grains of ~200-2000 μm; models still needed

evidence.quote: Further analysis with dust scattering models using the multiwavelength observations is still necessary to determine the maximum grain sizes.

why_this_method.value: Mosaicking two fields is safe because the emission lies within the inner third of the primary beams

evidence.quote: it is safe to mosaic these data (ALMA Helpdesk #12418, private communication)

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Depolarization attributed to grain property changes was disfavored; alternatives are disordered field or unresolved structure

evidence.quote: Therefore, we see no evidence that the depolarization zones are due to changes in the dust grains themselves.

limitations_admitted.value: Lack of short baselines limits recovery of extended field structure, especially around IRAS 16293B

evidence.quote: First, we lack observations on shorter baselines to trace fully the magnetic field morphology at large angular extents.

limitations_admitted.value: Stokes V unusable; Stokes I maps are dynamic range limited

evidence.quote: Both the individual and mosaicked Stokes I maps are dynamic range limited because IRAS 16293 is so bright

referee_caveats_inferred: Bridge density and mass depend strongly on assumed T and opacity, and propagate into B and v_A
Toy model assumes equal stellar masses, plane-of-sky geometry and a straight massless cylinder
Self-scattering interpretation is qualitative; no scattering model was fit
DCF sigma_v comes from a private communication and the velocity dispersion is not measured here
Nyquist-sampled angles are not independent, which affects the KS/AD p-values
